sanskrit: sā tu vidhvastavapuṣaḥ kaśmalābhihataujasaḥ dadarśa pathi gacchantī vasūn devān divaukasaḥ
english: While going along the path she beheld the Vasus, those celestial gods, their forms wasted away and their vigour crushed by affliction.

sanskrit: tathārūpāṃś ca tān dṛṣṭvā papraccha saritāṃ varā kim idaṃ naṣṭarūpāḥ stha kaccit kṣemaṃ divaukasām
english: Seeing them in such a state, the foremost of rivers asked: "Why have your forms thus perished? Are the dwellers of heaven well?"

sanskrit: tām ūcur vasavo devāḥ śaptāḥ smo vai mahānadi alpe 'parādhe saṃrambhād vasiṣṭhena mahātmanā
english: The Vasus, the gods, replied to her: "O great river, we have been cursed by the great-souled Vasiṣṭha in a fit of rage for a trivial offence."

sanskrit: vimūḍhā hi vayaṃ sarve pracchannam ṛṣisattamam saṃdhyāṃ vasiṣṭham āsīnaṃ tam atyabhisṛtāḥ purā
english: "For we all, heedless, once walked right past the foremost of sages, Vasiṣṭha, who was seated in twilight meditation in an unobtrusive spot."

sanskrit: tena kopād vayaṃ śaptā yonau saṃbhavateti ha na śakyam anyathā kartuṃ yad uktaṃ brahmavādinā
english: "In his anger he cursed us to be born in a womb. What the knower of Brahman has spoken cannot be otherwise undone."

sanskrit: tvaṃ tasmān mānuṣī bhūtvā sūṣva putrān vasūn bhuvi na mānuṣīṇāṃ jaṭharaṃ praviśemāśubhaṃ vayam
english: "Therefore you, becoming a mortal woman, bear us as sons upon the earth; for we cannot enter the inauspicious womb of ordinary mortal women."

sanskrit: ity uktā tān vasūn gaṅgā tathety uktvābravīd idam martyeṣu puruṣaśreṣṭhaḥ ko vaḥ kartā bhaviṣyati
english: Thus addressed, Gaṅgā said "so be it" to those Vasus and then asked: "Who among mortals will be the best of men to act as your father?"

sanskrit: vasava ūcuḥ pratīpasya suto rājā śaṃtanur nāma dhārmikaḥ bhavitā mānuṣe loke sa naḥ kartā bhaviṣyati
english: The Vasus replied: "The righteous king named Śaṃtanu, son of Pratīpa, will exist in the mortal world; he shall be our father."

sanskrit: gaṅgovāca mamāpy evaṃ mataṃ devā yathāvadata mānaghāḥ priyaṃ tasya kariṣyāmi yuṣmākaṃ caitad īpśitam
english: Gaṅgā said: "O gods of unblemished honour, my mind also agrees with what you have said. I will do what is pleasing to him, and this is your wish as well."

sanskrit: vasava ūcuḥ jātān kumārān svān apsu prakṣeptuṃ vai tvam arhasi yathā nacirakālaṃ no niṣkṛtiḥ syāt trilokage
english: The Vasus said: "You should cast our newborn sons into the water, so that our release from the curse may come swiftly, O you who flow through the three worlds."

sanskrit: gaṅgovāca evam etat kariṣyāmi putras tasya vidhīyatām nāsya moghaḥ saṃgamaḥ syāt putrahetor mayā saha
english: Gaṅgā said: "I will do this. Let there be provided for him a son; his union with me should not be fruitless, for he desires a son."

sanskrit: vasava ūcuḥ turīyārdhaṃ pradāsyāmo vīryasyaikaikaśo vayam tena vīryeṇa putras te bhavitā tasya cepsitaḥ
english: The Vasus said: "Each of us will contribute an eighth part of our own valour; with that valour your son — and his desired heir — will be born."

sanskrit: na saṃpatsyati martyeṣu punas tasya tu saṃtatiḥ tasmād aputraḥ putras te bhaviṣyati sa vīryavān
english: "That son of yours will never beget offspring among mortals; thus he will be without children of his own, though he will be mighty in valour."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ te samayaṃ kṛtvā gaṅgayā vasavaḥ saha jagmuḥ prahṛṣṭamanaso yathāsaṃkalpam añjasā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having thus made this compact with Gaṅgā, the Vasus departed with joyful hearts, their purpose fulfilled exactly as they had intended.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ pratīpo rājā sa sarvabhūtahite rataḥ niṣasāda samā bahvīr gaṅgātīragato japan
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then that king Pratīpa, devoted to the welfare of all beings, sat for many years on the bank of the Gaṅgā, engaged in prayer.

sanskrit: tasya rūpaguṇopetā gaṅgā śrīr iva rūpiṇī uttīrya salilāt tasmāl lobhanīyatamākṛtiḥ
english: To him came Gaṅgā, endowed with beauty and virtues, like the goddess Śrī made manifest, rising from the water in a form most enchanting to behold.

sanskrit: adhīyānasya rājarṣer divyarūpā manasvinī dakṣiṇaṃ śālasaṃkāśam ūruṃ bheje śubhānanā
english: She of divine form and noble spirit, her face radiant as the moon, seated herself on the right thigh of the royal sage as he sat in study, that thigh like the trunk of a śāla tree.

sanskrit: pratīpas tu mahīpālas tām uvāca manasvinīm karavāṇi kiṃ te kalyāṇi priyaṃ yat te 'bhikāṅkṣitam
english: The sovereign Pratīpa then spoke to that noble-minded woman: "What may I do for you, fair one? What is it that you desire?"

sanskrit: stry uvāca tvām ahaṃ kāmaye rājan kuruśreṣṭha bhajasva mām tyāgaḥ kāmavatīnāṃ hi strīṇāṃ sadbhir vigarhitaḥ
english: The woman said: "O king, foremost of the Kurus, I desire you — accept me. For the rejection of women who offer themselves in love is condemned by the good."

sanskrit: pratīpa uvāca nāhaṃ parastriyaṃ kāmād gaccheyaṃ varavarṇini na cāsavarṇāṃ kalyāṇi dharmyaṃ tad viddhi me vratam
english: Pratīpa replied: "O lady of excellent complexion, I would not out of desire go to another man's wife, nor to a woman of different caste, O fair one — know this as my sacred vow."

sanskrit: stry uvāca nāśreyasy asmi nāgamyā na vaktavyā ca karhi cit bhaja māṃ bhajamānāṃ tvaṃ rājan kanyāṃ varastriyam
english: The woman said: "I am not unworthy, nor am I one to be avoided or rebuked at any time. Accept me, O king — a maiden, the finest of women, who offers herself to you."

sanskrit: pratīpa uvāca mayātivṛttam etat te yan māṃ codayasi priyam anyathā pratipannaṃ māṃ nāśayed dharmaviplavaḥ
english: Pratīpa replied: "What you urge upon me would overstep the bounds for me. Were I to act otherwise than I have vowed, the violation of dharma would be my ruin."

sanskrit: prāpya dakṣiṇam ūruṃ me tvam āśliṣṭā varāṅgane apatyānāṃ snuṣāṇāṃ ca bhīru viddhy etad āsanam
english: "You have come and seated yourself on my right thigh, O beautiful-limbed one. Know, O timid one, that this is the seat reserved for children and daughters-in-law."

sanskrit: savyataḥ kāminībhāgas tvayā sa ca vivarjitaḥ tasmād ahaṃ nācariṣye tvayi kāmaṃ varāṅgane
english: "The left side is the place of a beloved wife, but you have not taken that seat. Therefore I shall not engage with you in desire, O beautiful-limbed one."

sanskrit: snuṣā me bhava kalyāṇi putrārthe tvāṃ vṛṇomy aham snuṣāpakṣaṃ hi vāmoru tvam āgamya samāśritā
english: "Become my daughter-in-law, fair one — I choose you for the sake of my son; for you came and took your place on the side belonging to a daughter-in-law, O slender-thighed."

sanskrit: stry uvāca evam apy astu dharmajña saṃyujyeyaṃ sutena te tvadbhaktyaiva bhajiṣyāmi prakhyātaṃ bhārataṃ kulam
english: The woman said: "So be it then, O knower of dharma — I will be united with your son. Out of devotion to you I will honour the renowned lineage of the Bhāratas."

sanskrit: pṛthivyāṃ pārthivā ye ca teṣāṃ yūyaṃ parāyaṇam guṇā na hi mayā śakyā vaktuṃ varṣaśatair api kulasya ye vaḥ prasthitās tatsādhutvam anuttamam
english: "Among all the rulers of the earth, you are the supreme refuge. Even in a hundred years I could not fully describe the virtues of this line — that peerless excellence which has proceeded from you all."

sanskrit: sa me nābhijanajñaḥ syād ācareyaṃ ca yad vibho tat sarvam eva putras te na mīmāṃseta karhi cit
english: "Your son must not question my lineage, O lord, nor must he ever question whatever I may do — your son should never inquire into any of this."

sanskrit: evaṃ vasantī putre te vardhayiṣyāmy ahaṃ priyam putraiḥ puṇyaiḥ priyaiś cāpi svargaṃ prāpsyati te sutaḥ
english: "Dwelling thus with your son, I will bring him joy; and through virtuous, beloved sons your son will attain heaven."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tathety uktvā tu sā rājaṃs tatraivāntaradhīyata putrajanma pratīkṣaṃs tu sa rājā tad adhārayat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having said "so be it," she vanished on the spot. The king, expecting the birth of a son, kept her words in his heart.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu pratīpaḥ kṣatriyarṣabhaḥ tapas tepe sutasyārthe sabhāryaḥ kurunandana
english: At this very time, O joy of the Kurus, the bull among kṣatriyas, Pratīpa, practised austerities together with his wife for the sake of a son.

sanskrit: tayoḥ samabhavat putro vṛddhayoḥ sa mahābhiṣaḥ śāntasya jajñe saṃtānas tasmād āsīt sa śaṃtanuḥ
english: To that aged pair was born a son — he was Mahābhiṣa; from Śānta was born Saṃtāna, and from him came Śaṃtanu.

sanskrit: saṃsmaraṃś cākṣayāṃl lokān vijitān svena karmaṇā puṇyakarmakṛd evāsīc chaṃtanuḥ kurusattama
english: Constantly remembering the imperishable worlds won by his own deeds in a former life, Śaṃtanu was ever a doer of righteous deeds, O best of Kurus.

sanskrit: pratīpaḥ śaṃtanuṃ putraṃ yauvanasthaṃ tato 'nvaśāt purā māṃ strī samabhyāgāc chaṃtano bhūtaye tava
english: Then Pratīpa instructed his son Śaṃtanu when he came of age: "Formerly a woman came to me, O Śaṃtanu, for your welfare."

sanskrit: tvām āvrajed yadi rahaḥ sā putra varavarṇinī kāmayānābhirūpāḍhyā divyā strī putrakāmyayā sā tvayā nānuyoktavyā kāsi kasyāsi vāṅgane
english: "If that woman of lovely complexion — a divine woman full of beauty and desire, seeking a son — comes to you in private, O son, you must not ask her who she is or to whom she belongs."

sanskrit: yac ca kuryān na tat kāryaṃ praṣṭavyā sā tvayānagha manniyogād bhajantīṃ tāṃ bhajethā ity uvāca tam
english: "Whatever she may do that you think should not be done, you must not question her. By my command, honour her who offers herself to you" — so he instructed him.

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃdiśya tanayaṃ pratīpaḥ śaṃtanuṃ tadā sve ca rājye 'bhiṣicyainaṃ vanaṃ rājā viveśa ha
english: Having thus instructed his son Śaṃtanu, and having consecrated him in his own kingdom, the king Pratīpa then entered the forest.

sanskrit: sa rājā śaṃtanur dhīmān khyātaḥ pṛthvyāṃ dhanurdharaḥ babhūva mṛgayāśīlaḥ satataṃ vanagocaraḥ
english: That wise king Śaṃtanu, renowned throughout the earth as a wielder of the bow, became fond of hunting and constantly ranged through the forests.

sanskrit: sa mṛgān mahiṣāṃś caiva vinighnan rājasattamaḥ gaṅgām anucacāraikaḥ siddhacāraṇasevitām
english: Slaying deer and buffaloes, that best of kings roamed alone along the Gaṅgā, that river frequented by siddhas and cāraṇas.

sanskrit: sa kadā cin mahārāja dadarśa paramastriyam jājvalyamānāṃ vapuṣā sākṣāt padmām iva śriyam
english: One day, O great king, he beheld a supremely beautiful woman, blazing in her form like the goddess Śrī herself standing before him.

sanskrit: sarvānavadyāṃ sudatīṃ divyābharaṇabhūṣitām sūkṣmāmbaradharām ekāṃ padmodarasamaprabhām
english: She was flawless in every limb, with fine teeth, adorned with divine ornaments, wearing fine garments, standing alone, her radiance equal to the interior of a lotus.

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā hṛṣṭaromābhūd vismito rūpasaṃpadā pibann iva ca netrābhyāṃ nātṛpyata narādhipaḥ
english: Beholding her, the lord of men was filled with delight, his hair standing on end; marvelling at the perfection of her beauty, drinking her in with his eyes, he could not be satisfied.

sanskrit: sā ca dṛṣṭvaiva rājānaṃ vicarantaṃ mahādyutim snehād āgatasauhārdā nātṛpyata vilāsinī
english: And she too, having seen the king of great splendour as he wandered there, felt affection and tenderness stir within her, and the graceful one could not be satisfied.

sanskrit: tām uvāca tato rājā sāntvayañ ślakṣṇayā girā devī vā dānavī vā tvaṃ gandharvī yadi vāpsarāḥ
english: Then the king spoke to her, addressing her with gentle, soothing words: "Are you a goddess, or a dānavī, a gandharvī, or an apsarā?"

sanskrit: yakṣī vā pannagī vāpi mānuṣī vā sumadhyame yā vā tvaṃ suragarbhābhe bhāryā me bhava śobhane
english: "Or a yakṣī, or a nāgakanyā, or a mortal woman, O slender-waisted? Whoever you may be, O radiant as the womb of the gods, become my wife, O beautiful one."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā vaco rājñaḥ sasmitaṃ mṛdu valgu ca vasūnāṃ samayaṃ smṛtvā abhyagacchad aninditā
english: Hearing the king's words, soft, gentle, and sweet, that blameless one, remembering the compact of the Vasus, approached him with a smile.

sanskrit: uvāca caiva rājñaḥ sā hlādayantī mano girā bhaviṣyāmi mahīpāla mahiṣī te vaśānugā
english: And she spoke words that gladdened the king's heart: "I will become your queen, O ruler of the earth, obedient to your will."

sanskrit: yat tu kuryām ahaṃ rājañ śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubham na tad vārayitavyāsmi na vaktavyā tathāpriyam
english: "But whatever I may do, O king, whether it seems good or ill, I must not be restrained, nor must anything disagreeable be said to me regarding it."

sanskrit: evaṃ hi vartamāne 'haṃ tvayi vatsyāmi pārthiva vāritā vipriyaṃ coktā tyajeyaṃ tvām asaṃśayam
english: "As long as things proceed thus between us, I will dwell with you, O king; but if I am restrained or spoken to disagreeably, I will assuredly leave you."

sanskrit: tatheti rājñā sā tūktā tadā bharatasattama praharṣam atulaṃ lebhe prāpya taṃ pārthivottamam
english: When the king said "so be it," O best of the Bhāratas, she experienced matchless joy upon obtaining that best of kings.

sanskrit: āsādya śaṃtanus tāṃ ca bubhuje kāmato vaśī na praṣṭavyeti manvāno na sa tāṃ kiṃ cid ūcivān
english: Having obtained her, the self-controlled Śaṃtanu enjoyed her as he desired, thinking "she is not to be questioned" — he said nothing at all to her.

sanskrit: sa tasyāḥ śīlavṛttena rūpaudāryaguṇena ca upacāreṇa ca rahas tutoṣa jagatīpatiḥ
english: The lord of the earth was fully pleased by her conduct and character, by her beauty, generosity, and virtues, and by her devoted attentiveness in private.

sanskrit: divyarūpā hi sā devī gaṅgā tripathagā nadī mānuṣaṃ vigrahaṃ śrīmat kṛtvā sā varavarṇinī
english: For she, the goddess Gaṅgā, the river flowing through the three paths, that woman of excellent complexion, had assumed a beautiful human form.

sanskrit: bhāgyopanatakāmasya bhāryevopasthitābhavat śaṃtano rājasiṃhasya devarājasamadyuteḥ
english: She had come and presented herself as a wife to Śaṃtanu, that lion among kings, equal in splendour to the king of the gods, whose desire had thus been brought to him by fortune.

sanskrit: saṃbhogasnehacāturyair hāvalāsyair manoharaiḥ rājānaṃ ramayām āsa yathā reme tathaiva saḥ
english: She delighted the king with loving pleasures and clever arts, with charming coquetry and grace; and as she rejoiced, so did he.

sanskrit: sa rājā ratisaktatvād uttamastrīguṇair hṛtaḥ saṃvatsarān ṛtūn māsān na bubodha bahūn gatān
english: The king, absorbed in love and captivated by the qualities of that most excellent of women, did not notice the many years, seasons, and months that passed.

sanskrit: ramamāṇas tayā sārdhaṃ yathākāmaṃ janeśvaraḥ aṣṭāv ajanayat putrāṃs tasyām amaravarṇinaḥ
english: Sporting with her as he wished, the lord of men fathered upon her eight sons, each of them radiant as the immortals.

sanskrit: jātaṃ jātaṃ ca sā putraṃ kṣipaty ambhasi bhārata prīṇāmi tvāham ity uktvā gaṅgāsrotasy amajjayat
english: Each son as he was born she would cast into the water, O Bhārata, saying "I am gratifying you" as she plunged him into the current of the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: tasya tan na priyaṃ rājñaḥ śaṃtanor abhavat tadā na ca tāṃ kiṃ canovāca tyāgād bhīto mahīpatiḥ
english: This was not pleasing to king Śaṃtanu, yet the lord of the earth said nothing to her, fearing that she would leave him.

sanskrit: atha tām aṣṭame putre jāte prahasitām iva uvāca rājā duḥkhārtaḥ parīpsan putram ātmanaḥ
english: But when the eighth son was born, as she made as if to laugh, the king, tormented with grief, spoke to her, longing to keep a son for himself.

sanskrit: mā vadhīḥ kāsi kasyāsi kiṃ hiṃsasi sutān iti putraghni sumahat pāpaṃ mā prāpas tiṣṭha garhite
english: "Do not kill him! Who are you? Whose are you? Why do you harm your sons? O murderer of children, do not incur so great a sin — stop, O infamous one!"

sanskrit: stry uvāca putrakāma na te hanmi putraṃ putravatāṃ vara jīrṇas tu mama vāso 'yaṃ yathā sa samayaḥ kṛtaḥ
english: The woman said: "O you who desire a son, best of those who have sons, I am not killing your son. But this agreement I made has now run its course, just as a garment wears out."

sanskrit: ahaṃ gaṅgā jahnusutā maharṣigaṇasevitā devakāryārthasiddhyartham uṣiṭāhaṃ tvayā saha
english: "I am Gaṅgā, daughter of Jahnu, attended upon by hosts of great sages. I have dwelt with you for the accomplishment of a divine purpose."

sanskrit: aṣṭeme vasavo devā mahābhāgā mahaujasaḥ vasiṣṭhaśāpadoṣeṇa mānuṣatvam upāgatāḥ
english: "These eight are the great and mighty Vasus, the gods; through the fault of Vasiṣṭha's curse they took on human birth."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ janayitā nānyas tvad ṛte bhuvi vidyate madvidhā mānuṣī dhātrī na caivāstīha kā cana
english: "There is no father for them on earth other than you, nor is there any mortal woman like me who could serve as their mother."

sanskrit: tasmāt tajjananīhetor mānuṣatvam upāgatā janayitvā vasūn aṣṭau jitā lokās tvayākṣayāḥ
english: "Therefore I took on human form for the purpose of bearing them. By fathering eight Vasus, imperishable worlds have been won by you."

sanskrit: devānāṃ samayas tv eṣa vasūnāṃ saṃśruto mayā jātaṃ jātaṃ mokṣayiṣye janmato mānuṣād iti
english: "This was the compact of the gods, the Vasus, which was made known to me: 'You shall release each one as he is born from his human birth.'"

sanskrit: tat te śāpād vinirmuktā āpavasya mahātmanaḥ svasti te 'stu gamiṣyāmi putraṃ pāhi mahāvratam
english: "Those Vasus have been released from the curse of the great-souled Āpava. Farewell to you — I will depart. Guard this son; he is a keeper of great vows."

sanskrit: eṣa paryāyavāso me vasūnāṃ saṃnidhau kṛtaḥ matprasūtaṃ vijānīhi gaṅgādattam imaṃ sutam
english: "This stay with you was arranged in the presence of the Vasus as part of their plan. Know this son, born of me, as Gaṅgādatta — given by Gaṅgā."

sanskrit: śaṃtanur uvāca āpavo nāma ko nv eṣa vasūnāṃ kiṃ ca duṣkṛtam yasyābhiśāpāt te sarve mānuṣīṃ tanum āgatāḥ
english: Śaṃtanu said: "Who indeed is this one called Āpava? And what was the misdeeds of the Vasus, by whose curse they all came to take on a human body?"

sanskrit: anena ca kumāreṇa gaṅgādattena kiṃ kṛtam yasya caiva kṛtenāyaṃ mānuṣeṣu nivatsyati
english: "And what has been done by this boy, Gaṅgādatta, on account of whose deed he will remain dwelling among mortals?"

sanskrit: īśānāḥ sarvalokasya vasavas te ca vai katham mānuṣeṣūdapadyanta tan mamācakṣva jāhnavi
english: "Those Vasus who are lords of all the worlds — how did they come to be born among mortals? Tell me this, O daughter of Jahnu."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca saivam uktā tato gaṅgā rājānam idam abravīt bhartāraṃ jāhnavī devī śaṃtanuṃ puruṣarṣabham
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed, Gaṅgā, the goddess, daughter of Jahnu, then spoke these words to the king, her husband, Śaṃtanu, that bull among men.

sanskrit: yaṃ lebhe varuṇaḥ putraṃ purā bharatasattama vasiṣṭho nāma sa muniḥ khyāta āpava ity uta
english: "The sage named Vasiṣṭha, who was obtained as a son by Varuṇa long ago, O best of the Bhāratas — that sage is also known by the name Āpava."

sanskrit: tasyāśramapadaṃ puṇyaṃ mṛgapakṣigaṇānvitam meroḥ pārśve nagendrasya sarvartukusumāvṛtam
english: "His holy hermitage, filled with herds of deer and flocks of birds, lies on the flank of Meru, king of mountains, covered with flowers of every season."

sanskrit: sa vāruṇis tapas tepe tasmin bharatasattama vane puṇyakṛtāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ svādumūlaphalodake
english: "There that son of Varuṇa, best among doers of virtuous deeds, performed austerities in that forest, O best of the Bhāratas, which abounded in sweet roots, fruits, and water."

sanskrit: dakṣasya duhitā yā tu surabhīty atigarvitā gāṃ prajātā tu sā devī kaśyapād bharatarṣabha
english: "The daughter of Dakṣa, known as Surabhī, exceedingly glorious — that goddess gave birth to a cow from Kaśyapa, O bull of the Bhāratas."

sanskrit: anugrahārthaṃ jagataḥ sarvakāmadughāṃ varām tāṃ lebhe gāṃ tu dharmātmā homadhenuṃ sa vāruṇiḥ
english: "For the benefit of the world that righteous-souled son of Varuṇa received that excellent wish-fulfilling cow, fit to be a sacrificial cow."

sanskrit: sā tasmiṃs tāpasāraṇye vasantī munisevite cacāra ramye dharmye ca gaur apetabhayā tadā
english: "That cow, dwelling in that forest of ascetics frequented by sages, wandered freely through the pleasant and sacred woodland, fearless."

sanskrit: atha tad vanam ājagmuḥ kadā cid bharatarṣabha pṛthvādyā vasavaḥ sarve devadevarṣisevitam
english: "Then one day, O bull of the Bhāratas, all the Vasus, with Pṛthu at their head, came to that forest, which was frequented by gods and divine sages."
